statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 15% (low), Stress 37% (moderate), Confidence 88% (high).
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold across the overnight block. A narrow evidence-based danger window is mapped to 13:30-15:00 UTC on 23 September, covering the US cash open and the S&P Global flash PMI release, where the forecast reaches the WATCH band.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes at a record with an orderly path; Tail low, Stress moderate on elevated yields and an open Iran file
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,732.40, up 0.82%, in a session whose internals were divergent: the Dow fell 0.36% and the S&P 500 finished flat while AI and semiconductor leadership carried the index. The cash path was orderly - the close sat roughly 38 points below the session high inside a 274-point range - and VIX fell 4.44% to 14.21, so there is no observed evidence of persistent one-way structure or failed retracements. Globex has reopened with NQ near 31,030 inside a tight 44-point range on thin volume. Cross-asset signals conflict rather than align: crude fell about 3% (WTI near $89.7, Brent near $98.4) on reports that Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, while the 2-year yield near 4.75% sits at its highest since July 2024 and the 10-year holds near 4.97% after hawkish Fed supply-shock commentary. That conflict, together with record diesel prices and narrow index breadth, lifts Stress into the moderate band without supporting an elevated Tail. No scheduled US macro release falls in the overnight block; the first catalyst cluster is the 13:30 UTC cash open followed by September flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC, which is where the forecast places its only WATCH hours.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock hours carry a published Claude assessment. The overnight and European block held a steady low-Tail, normal-mode regime with Tail between 11% and 13%. Tail stepped up around the 22 September US cash open, peaking at 21% in the 14:00 UTC hour as trend-up structure appeared, eased back to 14-17% through midday in mixed mode, then returned to 20-21% across the 18:00-19:00 UTC block before decaying to 16% into the cash close as the advance stayed orderly.
outlookSummary: The overnight block is scored in the low Tail band: no scheduled US macro, thin Asian liquidity and a low VIX support continued two-way conditions, with Iran and UN General Assembly headlines as the main gap channel. Conditional risk builds through the European morning and peaks in the 13:00-14:00 UTC block, where the US cash open and September flash PMIs coincide and the mapped state reaches WATCH. Risk is projected to decay through the New York afternoon provided the opening move retraces, with a modest lift into the power hour and a return to the low band across the CME maintenance break.
